A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MimIC study and contain the complete main paper and supplementary Sections 7–9. Text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MimIC benchmark results, ablations, alignment and hallucination analyses, including additional experiments in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including supplementary generalization, training-scale and LoRA-combination experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same attention-head shift vectors, query-dependent magnitudes, alignment loss and language-modeling loss. The operational training and inference procedures in Section 3.2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate VQAv2, OK-VQA and COCO, plus Flickr30k, MME, SEED-bench and MMMU-Pro in the supplement. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: zero/few-shot ICL, RICES, FV, TV, LIVE and LoRA. Supplementary comparisons also retain their existing LoRA variants.

E3.justification: Models, training sizes, validation splits, shot settings, metrics and budgets remain unchanged. The introduction's correction from 8B to 9B does not revise the experiment: Section 4.1 already specifies Idefics-9b in both versions.

E4.justification: Both retain the component and shot-count ablations, alignment and hallucination analyses, qualitative cases, and supplementary tests of alignment location, shift implementation and combination with LoRA.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains standard deviations across the same ICD shot settings. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement. For example, Table 1 retains Idefics-9b MimIC scores of 59.64, 52.05 and 114.89 for VQAv2, OK-VQA and COCO.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects an unnormalized exponential to softmax. Its added residual-form line restates an identity already present in supplementary Equation (6), but misplaces a parenthesis, leaving the subtracted standard-attention term outside the multiplier μ.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about approximating ICL, data and parameter efficiency, and multimodal performance. Conclusion edits do not change their meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including the performance ceiling discussed in Section 9.1, computational constraints in Section 9.2 and limited parameter capacity in Section 9.4.

D1.justification: Section 7 and Tables 6–7 retain the same prompts, optimizer settings, learning rates, epochs, LoRA configurations, precision and batch parameters. The code-access disclosure is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to earlier ICL and shift-vector methods remain unchanged. Changed citation backreferences reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: Limited edits repair the truncated 'ntion difference term' sentence in Section 3.2, standardize MimIC/ICL wording, and correct introductory wording and punctuation. The section structure and broader narrative are retained.

P2.justification: All seven figures and twelve tables are retained, with small spacing and positioning changes across the main text and supplement. Equation (2) gains an annotated display line that also causes local text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes normalization in Equation (2) and repairs broken prose, but introduces incorrect grouping in the equation's new final equality; supplementary Equation (6) retains the correct identity. These competing corrections and errors in the central explanation, with otherwise unchanged methods and evidence, leave the net quality direction uncertain.
